historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, rounded down; equity CAGR rejected as the anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (+6.3%) diverges from EPS 3yr CAGR (-17.2%) by far more than 30%. Book value grew because FY2023's $2.1bn debt-funded Uni-Select acquisition expanded the asset base and buybacks slowed to a trickle, while earnings fell from the FY2021-22 scrap/used-car-price peak. Equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: UNCHANGED from the October build: All CAGRs end at FY2025 (continuing ops). Start points FY2022 (3yr) and FY2020 (5yr) are whole-company including Self Service (~$600m revenue, high-margin in the 2021-22 scrap-price spike), so the revenue CAGRs understate continuing-ops growth by ~1pp and the EPS/FCF CAGRs overstate the decline somewhat. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2020 1,242 -> FY2025 813; FY2022 990 -> FY2025 813. Owner-FCF CAGR (-8.1% 5yr) is slightly below reported (-7.8%) because SBC rose from $29m to $34m while FCF fell -- SBC is immaterial at 0.25% of revenue, so this is noise rather than a signal. The real story is that FCF has fallen every year since the FY2020-21 working-capital-release peak while revenue grew: margin compression (EBITDA 15.1% FY2020 -> 10.3% FY2025 on the reported series) plus the Uni-Select integration. Since FY2025 the trend has worsened: TTM Sep-2026 revenue 13,508 (-1.0% vs FY2025) and reported FCF 610 (FY2025 847).

scenario_narratives.base: LKQ stabilises under a new CEO as a low-growth, cash-generative distributor, but from a lower base than thought in October. The German ERP disruption turned out to be the visible part of a wider European problem (Q3-2026 Europe organic revenue -9.8%, segment margin 4.7% vs 10.0%); Alvarez & Marsal and new European leadership restore service levels through 2027, but the lost volume is not assumed to return. Revenue falls ~2.5% in the year to September 2027 and then grows ~2-2.5% nominal (price and ADAS content offsetting a 1-3%/yr decline in repairable claims). GAAP EBITDA margin recovers from 8.6% to 10.5% by year 5 and stays there -- below FY2024 and well below FY2023. Capex normalises to 2%, acquired-intangible amortisation runs off, and the $3.4bn net debt is serviced from ~$0.75-1.0bn of unlevered FCF. No value is ascribed to any transaction: the strategic review was suspended on 2026-10-29.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are (1) claims stabilisation -- used-car values firming and insurance premiums easing mean fewer total losses, so repairable volumes stop falling; (2) Europe fixed by the new operator-CEO and A&M (segment margin back toward 10%+) or sold once it is presentable; (3) ADAS calibration (Elitek) and EV body-part salvage adding ~1pt of growth. Margins return to 12% (FY2023 level) by year 5, a year later than the October build assumed, growth runs 3-3.5% mid-horizon, terminal growth 2.5% and a 15x cap. With the strategic review suspended there is no near-term transaction route to this value; it has to be earned operationally, which is why its weight is lower than in October.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are structural: ADAS-driven accident avoidance and rising total-loss rates shrink the repairable-claims pool every year; EV mix erodes the high-margin mechanical categories; tariffs on imported aftermarket parts are absorbed rather than passed through; Europe's 2026 customer losses are permanent and the segment earns a mid-single-digit margin on a smaller base, never covering its cost of capital; Specialty continues to shrink after two goodwill impairments; and with the strategic review suspended there is no bid to put a floor under the shares. Revenue falls 4% then 2% then 1%, margin sits at 8-8.5%, growth is 1% thereafter at a 12x terminal cap. Leverage turns a modest EV decline into a large equity decline, which is why this scenario's value sits far below base despite positive cash flow throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: LKQ is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF stream from a mature, slowly shrinking distribution business, discounted at an 8% USD WACC with the cyclical and execution risks charged in the scenario paths and weights rather than the discount rate. GAAP EBITDA is used with the perennial restructuring charges treated as a real cost and one-off impairments stripped. Operating leases are an operating cost (ASC 842), so they are inside EBITDA and outside net debt. The share count is held flat because SBC (0.25% of revenue) is fully expensed; the house/street band is correspondingly narrow and the price sits below both, so band_position is negative (the market is paying less than even the fully-expensed value). This is an update of the 2026-10-02 build: the model, WACC, terminal assumptions, D&A, capex, tax, working-capital and years 3-10 growth are unchanged; the anchors were refreshed to the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, and year-1 growth, the EBITDA margin path and the scenario weights were re-judged on the Q3-2026 results, the withdrawal of guidance and the suspension of the strategic review. The base year is TTM to September 2026, so year 1 is the twelve months to September 2027. The weighted value remains well above the price; that gap rests on the margin recovering from ~8.6% to 10.5% -- at the bear path the shares are worth less than they trade for.
key_risks_to_valuation: No guidance and no settled management: FY2026 guidance was withdrawn and the new CEO does not start until 2026-12-15; his first outlook (likely with Q4 results, February 2027) could rebase margins, capex, the dividend or the portfolio, and is the single most important datum for the next update
Europe: Q3-2026 segment margin 4.7% vs 10.0%; the base assumes most of that is recovered by year 3. Every 1pt of group EBITDA margin is worth roughly $4-5/share of equity
Repairable-claims decline is structural (ADAS, total-loss rates) and runs faster than the 1-3%/yr the base assumes
Tariffs on Taiwan/China/Mexico-sourced aftermarket parts compress gross margin if pass-through is incomplete (North America gross margin % already down 0.7pt in 9M-2026)

Leverage: $3.42bn net debt plus $1.36bn operating leases against ~$1.2bn of ex-impairment EBITDA; covenant leverage 2.8x vs 4.0x maximum. A dividend cut to protect the balance sheet is plausible and would be value-neutral in this model but not to the share price

Terminal assumptions: the FCF cap binds in every scenario (14x base, 15x bull, 12x bear), so the exit multiple a buyer grants a declining distributor is a judgment the reader should test on the Assumptions sheet
Restructuring charges are treated as recurring; if they genuinely end, GAAP margins would be ~0.5-0.7pt higher than modelled
The strategic review is suspended, not cancelled: a resumed sale of Europe, Specialty or the whole company would change the frame (upside capped at a bid, or a disposal at a value-destroying price)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: TTM to 2026-09-30, continuing operations (FY2025 13,651 - 9M-2025 10,339 + 9M-2026 10,196). Self Service (Pick Your Part) was sold Oct-2025 and is in discontinued operations; FY2023-FY2025 and all 2026 periods in the Metrics CSV are restated continuing-ops. FY2022 and earlier are whole-company and NOT comparable (Self Service was ~$600m revenue). The Romanian operations (held for sale, closing expected Q4-2026, no cash consideration) are still inside this base; they are small and their exit is absorbed in the year-1 growth rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: 252.4m common shares on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (2026-10-22) plus ~0.1m for the basic-to-diluted gap (the Q3-2026 quarter was a loss so its diluted count equals basic at 252.9m weighted; the 0.1m gap is the Q2-2026 figure, carried). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks ($123m TTM) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow add-back, TTM to 2026-09-30 (FY2025 $34m - 9M-2025 $27m + 9M-2026 $27m; Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement). LKQ publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure; equity-award tax withholding has not been tagged since FY2019 and ran $0.4-7.6m/yr in FY2014-FY2018, so it is immaterial at ~0.05% of revenue and is not added. SBC is 0.25% of revenue -- the house/street band is narrow for this name.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-09-30: FY2025 $159m - 9M-2025 $119m + 9M-2026 $83m ($30m in Q3-2026). ~$1.5bn of the authorization remains and was extended to October 2028, but authorized is not spent. Dividends ($0.30/quarter, ~$305m/yr, declared again 2026-10-27) are a distribution of the unlevered flows modelled here and are not deducted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.2 -> cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.9% (9M-2026 interest expense $164m, ~$220m annualised, on ~$3.7bn debt), after-tax ~4.3%. Capital structure at market: equity ~$4.8bn vs debt $3.74bn -> ~44% debt. WACC = 0.56 x 10.2% + 0.44 x 4.3% = 7.6%, rounded up to 8.0% -- UNCHANGED from the October build (the lower share price raises the debt weight and mechanically lowers the computed WACC; that is not a reason to discount a deteriorating business at a lower rate, so the rounded 8.0% is held). The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the European execution risk and the claims-decline risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost, as US GAAP ASC 842 already presents them: operating lease cost (~$344m FY2025) is inside operating expenses and so inside the GAAP EBITDA the margin path is anchored to, and operating lease payments are inside operating cash flow. Operating lease liabilities ($1,361m at 2026-09-30: $256m current + $1,105m long-term) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases ($132m) are inside total_debt as the filer reports them. Sanity multiples must be lease-consistent: EV ex-operating-leases against post-ASC-842 EBITDA is the matching pair here (the leases are a cost in EBITDA, not a liability in EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is $23m at 2026-09-30 and NCI's share of profit is ~-$1m (immaterial). Deducted once, in the equity bridge, at book. Flows are modelled on consolidated GAAP EBITDA.
inputs.ebitda_basis: GAAP operating income + cash-flow D&A, continuing operations, with restructuring left in as a real, recurring cost but one-off goodwill and held-for-sale impairments stripped (they are non-cash write-downs of past purchase prices, not a forward cost). TTM Sep-2026: GAAP EBITDA $1,059m (7.8%) after $163m of impairments ($52m Specialty goodwill Q4-2025, $88m Specialty goodwill and $23m Romania held-for-sale in Q3-2026); $1,222m (9.0%) ex-impairments; company 'Segment EBITDA' $1,313m (9.7%). The Q3-2026 quarter alone ran 7.6% ex-impairments (Segment EBITDA 8.9%), with Europe's segment margin at 4.7% against 10.0% a year earlier and North America steady at 14.5%. FY2026 guidance was WITHDRAWN on 2026-10-23, so there is no management anchor for year 1; the path is built from the Q3 run-rate and the lapping of the German ERP disruption (go-live April 2026).
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 build, same model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical industrial'; leases, NCI and risk-once handled per the adaptations). The strategic alternatives review was SUSPENDED on 2026-10-29 (including the Specialty sale process), so the 'live corporate action' routing question raised in October is now moot: there is no deal to weight and the three scenarios remain fundamental paths. What changed since October: Q3-2026 results (Europe organic -9.8%, group organic -5.4%, GAAP loss on $111m of impairments), FY2026 guidance withdrawn, CEO departed (Salvatore Abbate starts 2026-12-15, interim Office of the CEO until then), head of LKQ Europe departed, Alvarez & Marsal retained for Europe, strategic review suspended. BASE YEAR: balance sheet 2026-09-30 and flows TTM to that date, so year 1 is the twelve months to September 2027 (not calendar FY2027), discounted one full period; the horizon has rolled forward one quarter from the October build. last_fcf ($576m) is the reported LEVERED owner FCF (OCF - capex - SBC, after ~$215m of cash interest; the 9M-2025 comparative includes ~$50m of Self Service FCF) and is an anchor for the reader; the engine's projected FCF is UNLEVERED, so the base year-1 FCF (~$740m) sits above last_fcf by roughly after-tax interest (~$160m), as it should. Covenant headroom: total leverage per the credit facility 2.8x against a 4.0x maximum -- the bear case is not a solvency case. Price: regular close, not after-hours; 52-week range 16.85-37.13, so the stock is near the bottom of its range. The qualitative Analysis JSON on disk at build time was still dated 2026-10-02 (pre-Q3); the Q3 facts here are read directly from the Q3-2026 10-Q and the 2026-10-23 / 2026-10-29 press releases (8-K exhibits 99.1).

bear.rationale: CHANGED: year-1 growth -2.0% -> -4.0% (the current organic run-rate persists through the year), and margin 9.2%/9.0% flat -> 8.0% for two years then 8.5% flat. The October bear's 9.0% floor is now simply the trailing-twelve-month actual, and the latest quarter is 7.6%, so it no longer describes a downside. Structural decline: ADAS keeps cutting accident frequency and total-loss rates keep rising, so North American repairable claims fall 2-4%/yr for several more years; the customers lost in Germany, the UK and Benelux do not come back and Europe stays at a mid-single-digit segment margin; tariffs on Taiwan/China/Mexico-sourced aftermarket parts are only partly passed through; Specialty keeps eroding. Years 2-10 growth, the 1.0% terminal growth and the 12x cap are UNCHANGED. Covenant leverage is 2.8x against 4.0x and the flows stay positive -- this is not a solvency scenario and the bear does not reach the zero-TV floor.

base.growth_rationale: CHANGED in year 1 only (-0.5% -> -2.5%). Year 1 is the twelve months to Sep-2027: group organic revenue ran -5.4% in Q3-2026 (Europe -9.8%, North America -2.4%), and the German ERP go-live was April 2026, so Q4-2026 and Q1-2027 still compare against pre-disruption quarters (Europe revenue stepped from ~$1,620m to ~$1,455m a quarter) before the comparison eases from Q2-2027; the Romania exit takes a little more. Roughly -5%, -5%, 0%, +1% by quarter gives ~-2.5%. Year 2 (+1.5%) through year 10 are UNCHANGED from October: ~2% parts inflation and rising ADAS/calibration content per repair against a continuing 1-3%/yr decline in repairable claims, no bolt-on M&A, and NO assumed recapture of the German volume lost in 2026. Terminal 2.0%.
base.margin_rationale: CHANGED across the path. GAAP EBITDA with restructuring left in and impairments stripped. TTM Sep-2026 is 9.0% on that basis and the Q3-2026 quarter ran 7.6%. Year 1 at 8.6%: Q4-2026/Q1-2027 near the Q3 run-rate with elevated restructuring (new CEO, A&M engagement in Europe), recovering through 2027 as German service levels are restored. The October path (9.7% -> 11.0% by year 5) is replaced by 8.6% -> 10.5% by year 5: the mature level is cut 0.5pt because Q3 showed the European problem is wider than the German ERP (volume declines in the UK and Benelux, 'heightened competition', lower vendor rebates, fixed-cost deleverage on a smaller revenue base), management's own lowered forecasts triggered goodwill tests on both Europe (only 20% headroom) and Specialty (impaired $88m), and North America's segment margin is 14.5%, not the 16-17% the October build leaned on. 10.5% remains below FY2024 (11.2%) and FY2023 (12.4%).
base.da_capex_rationale: UNCHANGED. D&A 3.0% of revenue (TTM Sep-2026 $411m) glides to 2.3% as the Uni-Select/Rhiag/Keystone intangibles run off. Capex 1.8% rising to 2.0%: TTM capex is only $186m (1.4%) as management squeezes spend, which is treated as under-investment rather than a new normal (FY2023-24 ran 2.3-2.7%). Would move on: a stated lower maintenance-capex level from the new CEO, or a site-network reduction in Europe.
base.tax_rationale: UNCHANGED at 27% of EBIT. Cash taxes paid / GAAP operating income: FY2023 23%, FY2024 28%, FY2025 30%; the 9M-2026 GAAP effective rate of 35% is inflated by non-deductible goodwill impairment and is not a cash-rate signal. Would move on: a sustained shift in profit mix away from Europe.
base.wc_rationale: UNCHANGED at -20% of the revenue change. Inventory $3.26bn + receivables $1.35bn against payables $1.92bn at 2026-09-30, so net working capital is ~20% of revenue and growth consumes cash; the year-1 revenue decline releases ~$70m, consistent with the $99m inventory release in 9M-2026.

bull.rationale: CHANGED in years 1-4 only: year-1 growth -0.5% -> -2.0% and year-2 2.5% -> 3.0% (the lost German volume is partly recaptured), and the margin ramp starts from 8.8% and reaches the unchanged 12.0% mature level one year later than in October. The mature assumptions are UNCHANGED: repairable claims stabilise (firming used-car values, easing insurance premiums), the new CEO and Alvarez & Marsal fix Europe or it is eventually sold, and the group margin returns to the FY2023 level of ~12%. Growth 3-3.5% in years 3-5 from ADAS calibration, EV salvage partnerships and modest European consolidation. Same WACC: the upside is in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: CHANGED from 30/50/20. Bear 35% (house default 15%): since October the company has printed a third consecutive shortfall, withdrawn guidance altogether, lost its CEO and its European head, impaired Specialty goodwill and seen Europe's margin halve; the claims decline is structural and the equity is levered. It is not higher because North America performed in line (segment EBITDA $203m vs $199m a year ago) and covenant leverage is 2.8x against 4.0x. Bull 15% (was 20%): the October build kept the bull at 20% explicitly because a live strategic review could deliver bull-case value without an operational turnaround; that review was suspended on 2026-10-29, so the bull now needs claims to stabilise AND an unproven new team to fix Europe AND margins to recover 3pt. Base 50%: stabilisation at a lower margin under new management is the central case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
